newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Markovic first Serb politician to visit Slovenia.
newsitem.headline: Markovic first Serb politician to visit Slovenia.

text.p: Mirjana Markovic, the high-profile wife of Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic, on Thursday became the first politician from rump Yugoslavia to visit Slovenia since the country gained independence in 1991.

Slovenia's Foreign Ministry said it had issued a visa for a one-day visit by Markovic, who leads the Yugoslav Left (JUL) party that is part of Yugoslavia's ruling coalition, to present the Slovenian translation of her new book "Response".
The book is a collection of interviews she has given to journalists over the past eight years.
"We gave her an ordinary visa and treated her as a visiting writer," Milivoj Butina, the head of the Foreign Ministry's consular department, told Reuters.

Markovic arrived in a government-owned Learjet, the first Serbian plane to land on Slovenian soil since the country's 10-day war of independence against Yugoslavia which claimed some 60 lives in 1991.
The book presentation was originally planned for the city of Trzic, about 50 km (31 miles) north of Ljubljana, but was moved to the capital following strong protests by the town's mayor.
"About 30 percent of people living in Trzic are of other Yugoslav nationalities and I was afraid of possible conflicts," the town's mayor, Pavel Rupar, was quoted as saying.
Police said the visit passed without any protests or security problems.
